title: Create RoomSwitcher and SceneControls React components
description:
Create react_ui/src/components/RoomSwitcher.tsx and react_ui/src/components/SceneControls.tsx implementing the UI for room switching (create room, list rooms, switch active room, delete room) and scene controls (start/end scene, pause/resume, update location/activity/tone/intensity, manage persona).

Before editing, inspect:
- AGENTS.md
- docs/plans_tasks.md
- docs/architecture.md
- react_ui/src/api/client.ts (updated by task b.8 — understand available API functions, TypesScript types, and call patterns)
- Existing react_ui/src/components/ files (understand React patterns, component structure, hook usage, and Tailwind styling conventions)

Do not infer APIs, constructor signatures, function names, module locations, or service topology from the task description alone. Inspect the referenced documents and existing implementation files first, then implement against the actual repository.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY react_ui/src/components/RoomSwitcher.tsx and react_ui/src/components/SceneControls.tsx. Do NOT modify any other file under any circumstance. Do NOT update documentation, READMEs, operations guides, or any code outside the listed paths. If you believe other files need updating, ignore that impulse and finish the task with only the listed files modified. Out-of-scope edits will cause the task to be rejected.

Implementation details:

--- react_ui/src/components/RoomSwitcher.tsx ---

1. A React functional component `RoomSwitcher` with Tailwind dark-theme styling:
   - Props: userId (string), activeRoomId (string | null), onRoomChange (callback: (roomId: string, roomType: RoomType) => void).
   - On mount, fetches rooms for the userId using listRooms API.
   - Displays a horizontal tab bar or vertical list of rooms, each showing display_name and a room type icon/badge (chat bubble for one_on_one_chat, theater mask for roleplay_scene, folder for project, heart for emotional_support, brain for memory_review).
   - Active room tab is highlighted with a distinct border/accent color.
   - Each room tab shows a small '×' button for delete (with confirmation dialog).
   - A '+' button at the end opens a create-room modal with:
     * room_type dropdown selector with labels for each type.
     * display_name text input.
     * companion_id optional text input.
     * Create and Cancel buttons.
   - Handles loading, empty (no rooms), and error states.

--- react_ui/src/components/SceneControls.tsx ---

1. A React functional component `SceneControls` with Tailwind dark-theme styling:
   - Props: roomId (string | null), roomType (RoomType | null).
   - When roomType is not 'roleplay_scene', renders nothing (return null).
   - On mount, fetches the active scene via getActiveScene API.
   - If no active scene exists, shows a 'Start Scene' button that opens a scene-creation modal:
     * location and activity text inputs (required).
     * Start Scene button.
   - If an active scene exists, displays a scene control panel:
     * Scene summary bar (location, activity, tone badge, intensity meter 1-10).
     * Pause/Resume toggle button.
     * End Scene button with confirmation dialog.
     * Edit button that expands inline editors for location, activity, tone (dropdown), intensity (slider), and scene_context (textarea).
     * Persona section:
       - 'Set Persona' button opens a modal with fields: name, description, traits (comma-separated input), voice_style, backstory, scene_goals (one per line), constraints (one per line).
       - On save, calls setScenePersona and displays the generated system prompt preview in a collapsible section.
     * Memory classification test: a small text input and 'Classify' button that calls classifySceneMemory and shows the result (scene_only / durable / both) as a color-coded badge.
   - Handles loading, empty, and error states.

SceneControls shows full control panel with pause/resume/end when scene is active
SceneControls has inline editors for location, activity, tone, intensity, scene_context
SceneControls has persona set modal and system prompt preview
SceneControls has memory classification test with result badge
Both components handle loading, empty, and error states
